messages:
Maria (AE): Customer dropped the SIG/CAIQ BCP section. They want explicit RTO/RPO, backup cadence, restore test evidence, failover mechanics, and our SLA language. Can someone draft concise answers and a small runbook excerpt for attachments?

Jordan (Security): I got this. We should split answers by Hosted vs Dedicated/Private and be conservative on numbers for hosted.

Sam (Eng): Quick facts to use: control plane metadata replicated cross-AZ, primary DB writes WAL-shipped to a standby in secondary region, object storage snapshot hourly, nightly full backups. KV caches are ephemeral and rebuilt on restart.

Jordan (Security): Draft text for SIG: Hosted: multi-AZ replication with automated snapshots. RTO objective (control plane): <= 1 hour for recovery of control-plane services; RPO for persisted customer metadata: 15 minutes (hourly backups with WAL shipping). Dedicated/Private: RTO/RPO are contract-configurable and can be tightened per SOW.

Jordan (Security): Failover mechanics: smart routing + health checks route traffic to healthy region/cluster automatically. For catastrophic region loss we activate cross-region DNS failover and promote standby cluster. Typical automated failover window: 1–5 minutes for routing; full recovery depends on restore size.

Sam (Eng): Backup cadence / retention to state in SIG: hourly incremental snapshots, nightly full backups retained 30 days by default. Longer retention or export snapshots available as an add-on. Restore testing: we run quarterly restore drills; can provide sanitized logs/screenshots as evidence.

Olivia (Legal): For customer-facing SIG answers include SLA callouts but avoid absolute promises outside the SLA. Suggested legal phrasing: "Hosted: Monthly uptime SLA 99.9%; Dedicated: 99.95% (see contract). Remedies subject to SLA terms, exclusions (customer misconfig, network third-parties), and force majeure."

Sam (Eng): Small runbook excerpt we can attach:

```
# Failover test steps (excerpt)
1) Notify: post in #eng-oncall and set maintenance flag in console
2) Trigger: flip routing flag to route traffic to secondary region
3) Smoke: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api-secondary.redwood.ai/health
4) Validate: check replication lag < 30s, verify sample requests succeed
5) Restore: re-sync primary from backups, monitor until steady
Evidence: attach screenshots, controller logs, and timestamped runbook entry
```

DR Playbook Bot: <https://runbooks.redwood.internal/dr-tests/2025|DR Playbook — failover & restore> :link: (added runbook link and last test index).

Maria (AE): This is great — I'll paste into the SIG spreadsheet and flag ops for the last quarterly restore artifacts.

Jordan (Security): I will pull the last restore test logs and scrub PII, will upload within 24 hours.

Olivia (Legal): LGTM. Keep hosted answers conservative and reference the SLA and SOW for any tightened RTO/RPO. :white_check_mark:

Maria (AE): Thanks team — I'll send to customer and loop back with any follow-ups.
